newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW - China-backed property issues favoured.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW - China-backed property issues favoured.

text.p: China-related property firms with strong support from mainland parents and quality assets are being favoured in Hong Kong's new issue market as investors try to limit their exposure to earnings growth risks, analysts said.
"The quality of their underlying assets, such as their locations, is the primary concern and parent back up is the second consideration," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
Because of ties with China parents and mainland authorities, analysts said these companies have more chance of participating in good quality and profitable property projects in the future.
The most attractive firms have assets in prime locations in major cities such as Shanghai and Beijing, or participate in redevelopment projects in old urban areas, analysts said.
"The listing response will also be good if their assets are in prime locations and their parents are strong," said Ben Kwong, research director at Dharmala Securities.
Analysts said they expected a strong response to China Resources Beijing Land Ltd initial public offering (IPO).
This was because of the company's presence in Beijing and its ties with mainland authorities through its China Resources Enterprise Ltd red chip parent.
Market sources said the local portion of the company's 300 million share IPO was over 100 times subscribed.

The company holds a 52 percent stake in a land development company in Beijing, which focuses on the reconstruction of old and dilapidated buildings in the Xicheng District of Beijing and large-scale residential developments around Beijing.

"Local investors like this kind of stock due to speculation that its parent will continue injecting more property assets at lower land costs into the company in the future," said Michael Ng, analyst at ASG Investment Services.
But analysts said the response to Concord Land Development Co Ltd's 300 million share IPO was expected to be cool.
The company is the property arm of Hong Kong-based Pacific Concord Holdings Ltd

It has eight property projects -- two in Hong Kong and six in China. The Chinese projects -- in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shuzhou, Shenyang and Wuhan -- are mainly shopping malls and commercial complexes.
Analysts said a growing supply of commercial properties in China in coming years would affect the earnings prospects of Concord Land.
But they said contributions from the projects was hard to predict because most of the projects are due for completion in about two to three years.
Expectations of a slow recovery in China's property market, because of an increase in supply, had made investors selective, analysts said.

"The China property market is seen recovering at a very slow but steady pace as we expect more supply of office property in coming years," said Patrick Chia, research manager at China Everbright Research.
Among upcoming IPOs, Hong Kong-incorporated China property development group Nam Fong International Holdings Ltd is expected to list by the end of 1996.
It engages in residential and commercial property developments in China's southeastern province of Guangdong, mainly in Guangzhou.
Winsor Industrial Corp Ltd demerged its property arm Winsor Properties Holdings Ltd and is expected to list the shares on November 8 by way of a market introduction.
Evergo China Holdings Ltd, a China property spinoff of Chinese Estates Holdings Ltd is expected to be listed by way of introduction on November 20.
